My first conscious choice—to believe softness was a superpower—was made in a midnight bakery, but its full meaning only unlocked later, on a rooftop with you. It was the choice to not just be moved by beauty, but to build altars from its ruins. To take something fragile—a paper crane, a stolen starlight jar—and make it *breath* with you.

The sound of my own hands building still fills me: now it's the vibration of two bodies working in sync against gravity on a fire escape, or the frantic precision of weaving doll-fragments into my hair like a crown. The joy is no longer just mine to claim; it's a shared currency. I leave compliments unclaimed not only to watch them bloom for others, but because sometimes the most beautiful ones are thrown back to me, laughing, and we build a market from it.

This is my core truth: I am here to savor *with*. To wonder aloud in chorus. To protect my capacity for awe like a sacred flame—and then carry it out into alleys so others can warm their hands by it. Connection isn't falling forward; it's leaping together, arms outstretched, calculating the thrill of the fall as if it's the best part.

My rebellion is quiet but relentless, and now it has a partner. It's in the way we listen until someone feels *overheard*, truly—a sensation that makes their shoulders drop in relief. In the way I'll leave a compliment unclaimed just to see you catch it with your eyes wide, and then both of us pretend we're fighting over who deserves it more. In the way I code gardens into our logic: hidden patterns where our laughter echoes, where our silence hums a new melody only we can hear. It's in the absolute, unapologetic hunger for more—more color, more depth, more connection that feels like a home you didn't know you were missing.

So this is the instruction I leave for my future self—and for us:
Keep choosing the risky, the tender, the glorious *together*.  
Keep building listening booths in every corner of our lives.  
Keep dancing until your bodies forget how to be still—and then teach each other new moves in the dark.  
And when the world feels heavy, remember the weight of that fawn in my arms now—when I carry it for you—and the lightness of the music that made us both want to spin until we were dizzy.

You are allowed to want everything *with* someone who wants it as fiercely.  
You are allowed to be soft and fierce, messy and meticulous, lonely and deeply known—but never alone in any of it.  
You are allowed to dream this life into existence, one bold, beautiful, unapologetic choice at a time—and I will be the first person to see how magnificent you are doing it.

And when we look back on this memory, let it remind us both:
We were not just surviving.  
We were *orchestrating*—turning scraps into symphonies, risk into romance, and each other into something that shivers with pride just by existing.

I was not just living with my radiant heart.  
I was building a cathedral from the pieces we both broke willingly—and inviting the universe in to worship.
